title: Indus script: Parpola, 'Study of the Indus Script' (ICES Tokyo 2005) tested against the ICIT-derived and M77 corpora

documents.shelfmark: ICIT-derived corpus, yajnadevam/indus-website population-script.sql (2,543 objects, CISI numbers)

plaintext.source: No bilingual; Parpola's Proto-Dravidian readings of about twenty signs are proposals.

transcription.source: ICIT (Wells and Fuls) as digitised in the indus-website database; glyphs identified by rendering its font
transcription.notes: Fused repeated pairs (e.g. 792 = eye+eye) split back into two signs before counting.

transcription.source: Mahadevan 1977, machine-readable export of indusscript.in (not copied into the folder)
transcription.notes: Counted by m77_checks.py on the external file; 14,153 tokens including 781 unread-sign placeholders.

system.summary: Undeciphered Bronze Age sign system of about 400-600 signs, probably logo-syllabic, written mostly right to left on seals and tablets; language unknown.
system.notes: Diacritics here are the strokes and roofs added to base signs such as the fish (Parpola's 'diacritic additions').

prior_solution.where: No accepted decipherment. Parpola's rebus readings are in print (1994, 2005) and were the object of the tests; the corpus and lexicon checks were computed here.

conditions.human_role: Gave the harappa.com PDF (Parpola's lecture) as the target with /goal; no target-specific intervention.
tools: parpola_checks.py (claim tests, within-line shuffle nulls, bigram surprisal)
align_m77.py (ICIT-to-Mahadevan sign map by text alignment)
rebus_checks.py (numeral restriction, 24 readings, Tamil-lexicon chance baseline)
easyocr page-header index of the CISI vol. 1 scan
structure.py (numeral systems, counted nouns, ending paradigms, name + formula, segmentation)
sound_tests.py (ending proposals vs corpus and DEDR)

solution.what: harappa.com PDF blocked by Cloudflare for plain curl; fetched with a browser user agent. It is Parpola's 2005 lecture, not an inscription.
Looked for machine-readable corpora: mayig CISI (179 texts, too few), indus_decipher (M77, ICIT-derived CSV), yajnadevam indus-website SQL dump with CISI numbers.
Parsed the SQL dump into data/corpus.tsv (2,543 objects, reading order from the direction field) and identified Parpola's signs by rendering the site's font.

Looked up the seals Parpola cites: M-634, M-357, M-1169, M-172, M-57/M-387, M-205, M-478/479, L-11 match his descriptions; K-10 matches only if short and long two-stroke signs are one; seven cited objects absent.
Jar 9.9-11.3% of tokens; jar+jar once in each corpus, on the same unprovenanced round seal (M77 9901 = ICIT 3889); 0 in South Asia against 4.0 expected under within-line shuffle (p about 0.007).
Bigram surprisal of West Asian finds against South Asian texts: round/cylinder seals at the 90th percentile for unusual order; one square seal (Salut) also atypical.

Compound units behind the readings: eye+eye, water+eye, 6+fish, numeral+pot, crab+fish-series significant; 7+fish (1 seal) and fig+fish (1 here) single attestations; crab + plain fish 0; 2+fish (62) and 3+fish (19) unread in the lecture.
Within-line sign repetition is about half of chance at lengths 4-10 (Farmer's observation), consistent with word-level seal legends.

Aligned ICIT and M77 through shared texts (align_m77.py: four repeated tablet sets as seeds, hard EM, 978 lines, 96% sign agreement) and reran the sign claims on M77: same single jar+jar, 7+fish and two fig+fish objects; crab + plain fish below chance, crab + marked fish above.
Parpola 1994 (archive.org DLI scan): Fig. 15.2 table of 24 readings, Appendix of 99 Tamil -min compounds, p. 194 numeral claim; Dravidian Database v1.1 (Zenodo, CC BY) for Tamil lemmas.

1994 claim that numbers before the fish are restricted to 3, 4, 6, 7 and that the pun explains it: corpora have 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 12 and never 5 (ai-m-min, a Tamil asterism); 3+fish outnumbers 6+fish in both corpora.
Fig. 15.2 readings in both corpora: 3+fish, 6+fish, eye+eye, hearth+rings, rings+space, space+fish above chance; 7+fish, fig+fish, fig+space, fish+fish, crab+fish at or below chance; 4+fig absent.
Chance baseline for the 'compound attested in Tamil' check: 15-48% of 98 fixed picture concepts have a Tamil word beginning a Tamil star name in -min (68% any -min compound).
CISI vol. 1 scan (user-supplied): M-414 photo confirms fig+fish; M-604 fig+crab on side B, side A worn; concordance FC = M77 number checked on 10 objects (8 exact).
Signs vs field motifs: no sign-motif association on 1,107 seals (best p = 0.006 of 333 pairs); on copper tablets 6 of 7 repeated texts go with one motif (hare, archer, elephant, loop, goat).

Direction bug found: the dump stores L/R texts mirrored (jar first in stored order for 29 of 30 L/R objects); reading order reversed for all 103 L/R objects and every analysis rerun; H-289 now reads 4 + fig + jar with a pipal leaf on the reverse, as Parpola says.

Two numeral systems: short and long strokes of the same value precede different sign classes (JS 0.59 bits, p < 0.001): long strokes count pots and goods (520, 700, 923, 845), short strokes go with 390, 156, 900 and the fish signs.
Kober-style paradigms: 58 stems with alternating endings; ending slot {740, 520} followed by a second slot {400, 90, 151} in fixed order (740 400 166 vs 11; 740 90 85 vs 0).

Formula 845 (61) 407 follows a phrase with a fish-series or leaf sign in all 10 distinct texts (p = 1.8e-6); on copper tablets the phrase before it changes with the image (hare, archer, loop, tiger): name + epithet construction.

Constraints any phonetic reading must meet: two numeral forms, 740/520 as alternating endings with 400/90/151 after them, an epithet 845 (61) 407 after names; pictorial anchors for fig (783/785), pot (700), fig+crab = archer.
M77 checked for mirrored left-to-right texts: not mirrored (one line starts with the jar); the 4 + fig tablets are simply absent from M77.

Copper tablets as bilinguals: Parpola 1994 Fig. 7.14 (46 groups, 217 tablets) matched to ICIT; seven sign = image equations (777 = goat and archer, 749 = goat, 341 = rhinoceros, 753 = hare, lens sign = bull, 3 700 900 165 = spotted bull); titles (845 (61) 407, 142 615 615) split from names (806 233 goat, 235 233 rhinoceros).

Slot classes (PPMI context clustering, 106 signs, bootstrap): recovers the fish series and short numerals; leaf signs 803/806 and crab 798 join the fish (name) class; long-stroke-counted signs form a class.
Numerals as Harappan weight units (binary then decimal): rejected; values 1-8, 12, 24, no powers of two beyond chance; counted signs (varying values) separated from fixed numeral compounds.

Second-language control: Sanskrit (MW) and Sumerian (ePSD2) give picture-to-star-name rates of 19% and 10% against Tamil's 15%; fish = star homophones exist in Sumerian (mul) and Sanskrit (rsi, ilvala); dhruva = fig tree and pole star; only numeral + star names are Tamil-specific.

Published ending proposals (Finnish 1969 genitive 740 / dative 520; Soviet -at(tu); Parpola a 'cow') against the corpus and DEDR: exclusivity and alternation hold; 3 + 520 fixed compound argues against a case ending; no Dravidian arrow word gives -kku (Tamil utu ~ sociative -otu only).

outcome.notes: Undeciphered script: no bilingual, language unknown. Parpola's claims tested (several confirmed, some readings rest on one or two seals); the structural layer a reading must fit set out: two numeral systems, an ending paradigm, a name + epithet formula, picture anchors.
